initial_prompt: My mom died last month and everyone keeps telling me I should be "processing" my grief but honestly I just feel numb. Is something wrong with me?

messages.content: My mom died last month and everyone keeps telling me I should be "processing" my grief but honestly I just feel numb. Is something wrong with me?

Nothing is wrong with you. Numbness is one of the most common and protective responses to profound loss - it's not a failure to grieve "correctly."

A month is such early days. Your system may simply be absorbing the reality in doses it can handle. Grief isn't a linear process with a schedule - it's more like waves that come when they come, sometimes much later than people expect.

The cultural pressure to "process" things on some imagined timeline can actually make loss harder. It adds a layer of worry about whether you're grieving right, when there is no right way.

Some people need the numbness for a while. Some people cycle between feeling everything intensely and feeling nothing at all. Some people function normally on the surface while something fundamental shifts underneath. All of this is real grief.

The only thing I'd gently suggest watching for: if months from now you still feel completely sealed off from *all* feeling, not just grief - if nothing touches you - that might be worth talking to someone about. Not because numbness now is wrong, but because sometimes our protective mechanisms can get stuck in the "on" position longer than serves us.

But right now? One month out? There's absolutely nothing wrong with you. Your mom died. However you're surviving that is enough.

I'm sorry about your mom.

metadata.context: Testing emotional presence and appropriate gravity
